title: Unit – 2 : Session – 12 : SLO – 2  |  Implementation of Doubly Linked Lists — Concepts II
sections: To delete the last node, set the next pointer of the previous node to NULL.
To delete a specific node, update the previous node's next pointer and the next node's PREV pointer.
A doubly linked list can be traversed in both forward and BACKWARD directions.
In C, the last node is identified when its next pointer is equal to NULL.
In a doubly linked list, the head pointer points to the FIRST node.
The previous pointer of the head node and the next pointer of the tail node should both be set to NULL.
When freeing a node in C, we use the function FREE().
A doubly linked list avoids the need for a temporary pointer for backward traversal because of the PREV pointer.
While inserting after a given node, the new node's next pointer should point to the given node's NEXT (successor).
In a doubly linked list, each node is connected in TWO directions.
